Evacuees From Oleshky Reach Ukrainian-Controlled Territory Amid Localized Ceasefire

01 Nov 2026, 04:27 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.dw.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysCivilians from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine have arrived in Kyiv-controlled territory after a complex evacuation effort. The town, located near the front line in the Kherson region, has been occupied since 2022 and faced a severe humanitarian crisis following the halt of food delivery supplies earlier this year.

Humanitarian Evacuation from Oleshky

Civilians from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine have arrived in Kyiv-controlled territory after a complex evacuation effort. The town, located near the front line in the Kherson region, has been occupied since 2022 and faced a severe humanitarian crisis following the halt of food delivery supplies earlier this year.

A localized ceasefire agreed upon by both sides allowed for the extraction of civilians from Oleshky. According to reports, participants had a choice to travel to Russia or proceed via Belarus to Ukrainian-controlled territory. Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets stated that the initiative involved extensive coordination, noting that early arrivals included infants and elderly residents alongside household pets.

Energy Infrastructure and Military Strikes Reported

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure across four Ukrainian regions left hundreds of thousands of households without electricity. Zelenskyy stated that the high intensity of the attacks aims to exploit shortages of interceptor missiles.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian military officials claimed responsibility for a strike on the Kamensky plant in Russia's Rostov region, stating that the facility produces solid fuel for rockets and missiles. Additional reported targets included military supply depots in occupied areas of the Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Luhansk regions.

In Russia, Nizhny Novgorod Governor Gleb Nikitin reported a massive overnight drone attack that caused significant damage to an industrial facility east of Moscow, though preliminary information indicated no casualties. Unconfirmed Ukrainian media reports identified the target as the Kstovo oil refinery. These battlefield claims have not been independently verified.

Diplomatic and Security Developments

  • Peace Talks Format: Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated that Russia prefers initial renewed peace negotiations to involve only Moscow, Kyiv, and Washington in a trilateral format.
  • G20 Foreign Ministers Meeting: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul commented on diplomatic engagement during the G20 meetings in Atlanta, noting that Western nations and the US remain aligned while omitting a traditional group photo due to the presence of Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
  • Istanbul Meetings: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy traveled to Istanbul to meet with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to discuss Black Sea shipping and diplomatic prospects.
  • US Security Warning: The US embassy in Moscow issued an alert regarding a credible threat of a mass-casualty plot targeting the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, prompting coordination with Russian law enforcement.

Practical Implications and Verification

Observers seeking to verify ongoing developments can consult official statements from the Ukrainian government, international monitors, and verified updates from humanitarian organizations assisting displaced persons. Independent verification of specific military strikes and casualty figures remains challenging due to active hostilities.
